item.title: Council on Human Reproductive Technology approves full resumption of services at "Heal Fertility Limited"
item.description:
The following is issued on behalf of the Council on Human Reproductive Technology:
      
     The Council on Human Reproductive Technology (Council) convened a special meeting today (October 5) to review the licence of "Heal Fertility Limited" (Heal Fertility). In view of the earlier incident involving a mix-up in embryo biopsy specimens at Heal Fertility, Council members thoroughly reviewed the information obtained from a follow-up on-site inspection, and confirmed that Heal Fertility has properly implemented all remedial and improvement measures. Therefore, the Council allowed Heal Fertility to fully resume all 17 treatment services covered by its licence starting tomorrow (October 6).
      
     Since July 8, the Council had suspended Heal Fertility's 14 treatment services out of 17, with the exception of three services related to the storage of gametes or embryos, and had set up an investigation committee to investigate the matter. The Council had convened a special meeting on September 3 to review the investigation report and the licence matters of Heal Fertility.  
      
     This meeting followed up on a special meeting held by the Council on September 3 regarding the same incident. At that time, the Council accepted its conclusion that the main cause of the incident may involve intentional unlawful conduct by an individual, and considered that there is still room for further enhancement in Heal Fertility's overall performance and operational arrangements following the incident. Consequently, on September 4, the Council sent a letter to Heal Fertility, explicitly requiring Heal Fertility to duly carry out a set of concrete improvement measures to prevent a recurrence of similar incidents. Until Heal Fertility had properly implemented the measures, it could only continue to provide three services related to the storage of gametes or embryos. 
      
     On September 22, the Council conducted another unannounced on‑site inspection of Heal Fertility, focusing on all aspects of the remedial measures.
      
     The Council was satisfied and convinced that Heal Fertility had refined its internal sample‑handling procedures, strengthened staff training, and upgraded laboratory management and security systems in accordance with the Council's requirements, including the implementation of CCTV surveillance on the premises, the installation of biometric locks on all cryostorage tanks, and the enhancement of sample identification and verification. The Council also noted that the main personnel involved in the incident had already left Heal Fertility, and that Heal Fertility has recruited new staff and provided training. After thoroughly reviewing the relevant reports and inspection results, the Council therefore allowed Heal Fertility to resume normal operations starting tomorrow. The Council will continue to closely monitor Heal Fertility's performance to safeguard the continuous provision of safe and high-quality services to individuals seeking human reproductive technology services.
      
     Moreover, the Council has commenced a review of the Code of Practice on Reproductive Technology and Embryo Research. Key areas include reviewing the incident reporting mechanism and optimising the security and handling procedures of biological samples, with a target completion date of next year.

item.title: Guard against fake messages claiming direct whole-day use of new Huanggang Port for vehicles under Guangdong-Hong Kong Regular Quotas
item.description:
A Government spokesman today (October 5) urged the public not to be misled by fake messages on social media that claim vehicles of Guangdong-Hong Kong Regular Quota holders issued with Closed Road Permits (CRPs) for the Heung Yuen Wai/Liantang Port, Shenzhen Bay Port or Sha Tau Kok Control Point (collectively referred to as designated control points) can directly use the new Huanggang Port to cross the boundary throughout the day. The case will be referred to law enforcement agencies for follow-up.

     Applicants for the Guangdong-Hong Kong Regular Quotas must currently satisfy the application qualifications set by the Mainland authorities and submit designated application documents (such as business registration documents in Guangdong and Hong Kong) to the Mainland authorities to apply for the Regular Quotas. Upon the issuance of the Approval Notice to applicants by the Mainland authorities, they may apply to the Transport Department of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region (HKSAR) Government for CRPs for the land control points endorsed on the Approval Notice. Vehicles with CRPs for the above designated control points are only permitted to travel between Guangdong and Hong Kong via the existing Lok Ma Chau Control Point or the soon-to-open new Huanggang Port between 0.00am and 6.30am daily.

     "Similar false information has surfaced from time to time in social media and messaging groups, repeatedly impersonating government announcements and falsely claiming that quotas are free from control point or eligibility restrictions to solicit clients. Such claims are particularly misleading to road users of both places amid the anticipated upcoming opening of the new Huanggang Port. The public should exercise heightened vigilance," the spokesman added.

     The HKSAR Government reiterated that arrangements regarding Guangdong-Hong Kong Regular Quotas and use of control points are serious issues which must be jointly deliberated by the governments of the two places holistically. There are currently no plans to adjust the arrangement of enabling cross-boundary vehicles with CRPs for designated control points to use the Lok Ma Chau Control Point/new Huanggang Port during the overnight period. Members of the public should refer to official announcements, especially regarding the opening arrangements for the new Huanggang Port, and verify messages carefully to guard against deception and avoid disruptions to travel plans.

item.title: Brussels ETO strengthens trade ties with Burgundy wine industry in France (with photos)
item.description:
The Hong Kong Economic and Trade Office in Brussels (Brussels ETO), in collaboration with the Hong Kong Trade Development Council (HKTDC), visited the Burgundy wine region in France from September 28 to 30 (Burgundy time) to promote Hong Kong's role as an international hub for wine trading.

     The visit covered key wine-producing areas in the Burgundy wine region. The Brussels ETO and the HKTDC held a number of meetings with the local government, wine producers as well as wine industry institutions to promote the vast opportunities in Hong Kong as the hub for wine trading, distribution and auction, and to exchange views on the latest developments in the global wine market as well as the local wine production industry.

     Speaking during a networking and promotional dinner with senior regional officials and industry representatives, the Special Representative for Hong Kong Economic and Trade Affairs to the European Union, Ms Shirley Yung, highlighted Hong Kong's standing as a world-leading hub for wine trading and auction, following the removal of wine duty in 2008 and the reduction of liquor duty in 2024.

     "Hong Kong's wine trading and auction activities are giving impetus to the development of other high value-added sectors such as logistics and storage, tourism as well as premium food and beverage consumption. We very much welcome the Burgundy wine trade to leverage Hong Kong's strategic position as the regional trading, distribution and auction hub to expand its market share in China and the wider Asia-Pacific region," Ms Yung added.

     During the visit, Ms Yung also extended her warm invitation to the Burgundy wine industry to visit Hong Kong, including for the Hong Kong Wine & Dine Festival in October every year, as well as the Hong Kong International Wine & Spirits Fair in November every year. Moreover, she promoted the Festival of Connoisseurs to the local wine industry, which will have its inaugural edition in November 2026 to showcase the art of premium lifestyles in Hong Kong.

     Burgundy is one of the world's most renowned wine regions, with a rich winemaking heritage rooted in its distinctive terroirs and traditions. About half of its wine is exported to international markets. The visit formed part of the Brussels ETO's ongoing efforts to foster exchanges between Hong Kong and Europe in the wine sector and identify opportunities for closer collaboration in wine business and wine tourism.

item.title: Import of poultry meat and products from areas in US and UK suspended
item.description:
The Centre for Food Safety (CFS) of the Food and Environmental Hygiene Department announced today (October 5) that in view of notifications from the World Organisation for Animal Health (WOAH) about outbreaks of highly pathogenic H5N1 avian influenza in Big Stone County and Kandiyohi County of the State of Minnesota, Ravalli County of the State of Montana, and Barron County of the State of Wisconsin in the United States (US), and a notification from the Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs of the United Kingdom (UK) about an outbreak of highly pathogenic H5N5 avian influenza in the Isle of Lewis of Scotland in the UK, the CFS has instructed the trade to suspend the import of poultry meat and products (including poultry eggs) from the above-mentioned areas with immediate effect to protect public health in Hong Kong.
      
     A CFS spokesman said that according to the Census and Statistics Department, Hong Kong imported about 24 190 tonnes of chilled and frozen poultry meat and about 20.2 million poultry eggs from the US, and about 340 tonnes of chilled and frozen poultry meat from the UK in the first six months of this year.
      
     "The CFS has contacted the American and British authorities over the issues and will closely monitor information issued by the WOAH and the relevant authorities on the avian influenza outbreaks. Appropriate action will be taken in response to the development of the situation," the spokesman said.

item.title: SCS visits Government Property Agency (with photo)
item.description:
The Secretary for the Civil Service, Mrs Ingrid Yeung, visited the Government Property Agency (GPA) this afternoon (October 5) to learn about the department's work in managing government properties and leveraging technology to enhance the quality and efficiency of services. She also met and exchanged views with staff representatives from various grades in the department.

     Accompanied by the Permanent Secretary for the Civil Service, Ms Shirley Lam, Mrs Yeung first met with the Government Property Administrator, Mr Raymond Sy, and other directorate staff, and received a briefing on the latest developments of the department's work on the use of government properties and enhancement of public spaces in joint-user government office buildings among other matters.

     Mrs Yeung then met with staff of the Property Management Division to learn about the latest situation of the management of government properties, including the preparatory work for the Hong Kong Port Area of the Huanggang Port Building conducted by the multidisciplinary team responsible for property management of the redeveloped Port. Mr Sy said that the department's staff have been working as one, in collaboration with the Security Bureau and other relevant departments, to ensure comprehensive preparation for the smooth opening of the Port.

     During the visit, the GPA staff introduced to Mrs Yeung the department's latest research and development in technology applications that aim to leverage AI to assist in the processing of large volumes of property management invoices and applications for repair and maintenance of property facilities, including the extraction and verification of data. This not only reduces the work of manual data input and checking to streamline workflow, but also enhances the accuracy of the vetting process. Staff can allocate their time more flexibly to follow up on complex cases and improve service quality.

     Mrs Yeung also watched a demonstration by staff of the Management Services Division of the in-house developed Mobile Site Inspection System (MSIS), a mobile application used in daily property inspections. The MSIS ensures standardisation of inspection items by listing the items to be inspected, while its report generation function not only streamlines writing and unifies report formatting, but also facilitates the systematic organisation of property inspection information. After processing by AI, the data will be uploaded to the government cloud, enabling staff to make use of big data analysis to study ways to further optimise services. Unlike in the past when paper documents such as property plans had to be carried during property inspections, staff now only need a tablet installed with the MSIS to view relevant property information, fill in inspection records, and take and upload inspection photos in a one-stop manner, with the application promptly generating an automated draft inspection report.

     Mrs Yeung said, "Hong Kong's First Five-Year Plan proposes to leverage AI technology to reform public administration. I encourage policy bureaux and departments to adopt an innovative spirit, integrate workflow, enhance overall efficiency, and build a more professional and efficient civil service." 

     Before concluding her visit, Mrs Yeung met with staff representatives from various grades in the department to exchange views on matters of concern to them.

item.title: HKSAR LegCo strongly opposes and disapproves of remarks by UK FCDO official on Hong Kong Alliance case
item.description:
The following is issued on behalf of the Legislative Council Secretariat:

     A spokesperson for the Legislative Council (LegCo) of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region (HKSAR) today (October 5) expressed strong opposition to and disapproval of the untruthful remarks made by an official of the Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO) of the United Kingdom (UK) responsible for Indo-Pacific affairs regarding the sentencing of the "Hong Kong Alliance" case. In a recent letter reply to members of the UK Parliament, the official smeared Hong Kong's judicial system and interfered in Hong Kong's affairs.
 
     The LegCo spokesperson stated that Hong Kong is a society underpinned by the rule of law. LegCo firmly supports the Court of First Instance of the High Court in handing down sentences in the case in accordance with the law, considering that the judgment demonstrates legal justice and strongly safeguards the HKSAR's constitutional order established by the Constitution of the People's Republic of China (PRC) (the Constitution) and the Basic Law of the HKSAR of the PRC (the Basic Law). LegCo resolutely opposes any foreign forces making malicious smears, slanderous attacks, and taking the opportunity to interfere in China's internal affairs regarding the case.
 
     The LegCo spokesperson reiterated that, as pointed out earlier by the HKSAR Government in response to the UK's so-called six-monthly report on Hong Kong, the core essence of the Sino-British Joint Declaration is about China's resumption of the exercise of sovereignty over Hong Kong. It did not authorise the UK to interfere in Hong Kong's affairs after its return to the motherland. Thereafter, the UK has no sovereignty, jurisdiction or right of supervision over Hong Kong.
 
     The LegCo spokesperson pointed out that the allegation, which was made by the UK FCDO's official responsible for Indo-Pacific affairs, that the defendants in the case were convicted merely for "peaceful acts of remembrance" completely disregards facts and misleads the public. The court pointed out in its reasons for sentence that the defendants were not on trial for their political thoughts or acts prior to the implementation of the Hong Kong National Security Law (HKNSL). The convictions were purely because, after the HKNSL came into effect, they continued to pursue the goal of overthrowing and undermining the leadership of the Communist Party of China (CPC) as established under the Constitution by committing various incitement criminal acts. Those acts attempted to cause Hong Kong citizens to lose trust in the Communist Party, thereby achieving the objective of undermining the fundamental system of the state, gravely endangering national security. The UK official's attempt to glorify criminal acts endangering national security as peaceful activities is a blatant trampling on the spirit of the rule of law.
 
     The LegCo spokesperson also reiterated that the Constitution is the fundamental law of the state, clearly specifying that the CPC's leadership is the core and foundation of the state's constitutional order. No country's constitution allows its citizens to subvert the established constitutional order and fundamental system of the state. The UK itself maintains various stringent laws safeguarding national security, yet makes unreasonable criticisms against the legitimate measures of the HKSAR in safeguarding national security in accordance with the law. This is a typical act of hypocrisy with double standards. The LegCo spokesperson requests the British side immediately stops the acts of interfering in Hong Kong's affairs.
 
     In fact, since the implementation of the HKNSL and the Safeguarding National Security Ordinance, the cornerstone of Hong Kong's rule of law has become more solid, and the various freedoms lawfully enjoyed by citizens have received more substantial protection. Various international indicators and rankings show that Hong Kong is a safe and stable city suitable for living and investment. As an integral member of the HKSAR's governing team, LegCo firmly supports the HKSAR Government in fully and faithfully implementing laws safeguarding national security, safeguarding high-quality development of the country and Hong Kong with high-level security, and ensuring the steadfast and successful implementation of the "one country, two systems" principle.

item.title: HKMA hosts CargoX Solution Day to promote regional trade data connectivity (with photos)
item.description:
The following is issued on behalf of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority:
 
     The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) today (October 5) successfully organised the CargoX Solution Day. The event served as a platform for key stakeholders in the cargo and trade data ecosystem to exchange insights and showcase the innovative solutions in enhancing trade data connectivity to regional levels under the CargoX Pilot Programme.
      
     Themed "From local to regional trade data connectivity: shaping the future of trade finance through innovative CargoX pilots", the Solution Day attracted over 300 industry professionals from banks, cargo and trade data providers, government agencies and partners of Commercial Data Interchange (CDI). The event featured keynote speeches, panel discussions and solution presentations, focusing on strengthening trade data connectivity with Hong Kong's key trading partners, such as the Chinese Mainland and the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) economies, as well as integrating CDI with key government cargo and trade data platforms.
      
     A highlight of the CargoX Solution Day was the signing of a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) between the HKMA and the PAA Digital Trade Alliance (PAA) (Note 1) to promote trade finance digitalisation. The two parties will commence joint innovation projects on enhancing cargo and trade data connectivity between Hong Kong and PAA member economies, thereby catalysing data-driven innovation in financial services and enhancing trade finance availability in the region.
      
     During the Solution Day, the HKMA also shared results achieved under the CargoX Pilot Programme, particularly its progress in enhancing connectivity with key trade corridors. In collaboration with the Shanghai Data Bureau (SDB), the HKMA has successfully established a link-up between CDI and a digital trade platform developed by the SDB. Known as "CargoX Connect", this collaboration has enabled five pilot banks (Note 2) to access and utilise trade declaration data from the Yangtze River Delta region, serving as the first pilot cohort. This development facilitates various trade finance processes, such as trade verification and due diligence on trade counterparts, resulting in faster loan drawdowns for Hong Kong businesses engaging in both onshore and offshore trade. To date, this pilot has enabled the approval of ten trade finance loans amounting to HK$180 million. The HKMA intends to extend this successful model to other provinces and cities in the Chinese Mainland as the next phase of development.
      
     Building on these encouraging developments in collaboration with the SDB and the PAA, through CargoX, the HKMA will continue to leverage Hong Kong's role as a super-connector to strengthen trade data connectivity along key corridors, including the Chinese Mainland and ASEAN. The ultimate goal is to enhance the transparency of cross-border trade transactions, thereby unlocking trade finance opportunities and supporting the growth of small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in the region.
      
     Deputy Chief Executive of the HKMA Mr Howard Lee said, "Today's CargoX Solution Day serves as a vital platform to showcase how the CargoX Pilot Programme is translating strategic recommendations into tangible actions. Building on the encouraging progress of the CargoX pilot projects, the signing of the MoU with the PAA marks a significant milestone in our endeavour to enhance regional trade data connectivity, including ASEAN economies, for more streamlined SME trade financing. By leveraging our CDI data infrastructure, CargoX will continue to expand from local to regional levels, building a more efficient and inclusive digital trade ecosystem across borders. This ultimately contributes to SME growth and fosters seamless international trade."
      
     The Chair of the PAA, Tan Sri Syed Zainal Abidin Syed Mohamed Tahir, said, "The signing of this MoU with the HKMA marks a transformative step forward for cross-border trade finance in the region. By seamlessly bridging the PAA's robust regional network with Hong Kong's cutting-edge CDI infrastructure, we are unlocking the true power of data-driven finance. Together, we will eliminate the traditional frictions in international trade, giving SMEs across ASEAN and neighbouring economies unprecedented access to capital. We are excited to co-create a more inclusive, resilient, and fully digitised regional trade ecosystem."

Note 1: The PAA is a global alliance comprising trade single window operators and e-commerce service providers from 15 economies, including ASEAN member states.

Note 2: These pilot banks include Bank of China (Hong Kong), Hang Seng Bank, The Hongkong and Shanghai Banking Corporation, Industrial and Commercial Bank of China (Asia) and Standard Chartered Bank (Hong Kong).

item.title: Advisory Council on the Environment fully supports Hong Kong's First Five Year Plan to continue to drive green transition in Hong Kong
item.description:
The following is issued on behalf of the Advisory Council on the Environment:

     The Advisory Council on the Environment (ACE) discussed at its meeting today (October 5) the major strategies and initiatives on environmental protection and related issues set out in the First Five-Year Plan for Economic and Social Development of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region (2026-2030) (Hong Kong’s First Five-Year Plan) and the Chief Executive's 2026 Policy Address (Policy Address). The ACE unanimously supports the strategies and initiatives.

     The ACE is pleased to note that four of the five binding indicators set out in Hong Kong's First Five-Year Plan are environment-related, covering carbon intensity, the share of zero-carbon energy, the average concentration of fine suspended particulates (PM2.5), and Hong Kong’s surface water quality, demonstrating the Government’s determination to build Hong Kong into a green and liveable city and drive its future green transition. At the meeting, members had in-depth discussions on various environmental protection and ecological issues and offered recommendations to the Government.  

     The Chairman of the ACE, Professor John Chai, said, "The ACE believes that the Government will implement various measures in accordance with Hong Kong’s First Five-Year Plan and the Policy Address to push forward Hong Kong’s green transition and foster green innovation continuously, thereby aligning with the National 15th Five-Year Plan. These efforts will contribute to building a Beautiful China and a Beautiful Hong Kong, as well as realising the green transition and high-quality economic development of the nation."

     Professor Chai added that the ACE will continue, as always, to provide professional advice to the Government on various environmental issues and drive the implementation of sustainable development and green transition in Hong Kong. The ACE will fully support and align with Hong Kong’s First Five-Year Plan, actively contributing to the future development of both the nation and Hong Kong.
